Concept · not live yet

Book the Room is a working concept, not a live feature.

Everything here is clickable so you can feel how it could work. We’re still early on this, in conversations with publishers, coordinators, and teams to really understand how to make this pain point simpler for everyone. There’s a lot of nuance to how sessions, scheduling, and splits actually come together, and we’re taking all of it in. This one is a ways out, so honest feedback right now is exactly what shapes it.

How it works

One system. Two surfaces. Zero double-entry.

Songwriters live in the We Should Write Sometime app. You see and act on everything here in the portal. Every connection, co-write, song and split flows between the two automatically — nothing is managed twice.

1

In the app · songwriters generate the data

Three everyday actions create everything the portal needs. Writers never fill out a form for you.

🔗Connect

Swipe, match & connect

Writers find each other by skill, city and style, then match and connect — building a living map of who actually writes with whom.
In person at a write or a show? Share your QR code — they scan, you both swipe right, connected.
→ becomes your Your Network
📅Schedule

Book the co-write

Shared availability suggests times that work for everyone. One tap to accept and the session lands on every writer's calendar.
→ becomes Sessions & bookings
🎵Manage & split

Songs, audio & splits

Each song holds its co-writers, audio, lyrics and writer + publisher splits, with a full change history and e-sign-ready split sheets.
→ becomes your Catalog, Insights & Split Sheets
▼

It stays in step, both ways

Change a split in the app and the portal flags it for review. Adjust a room or a split sheet in the portal and the writer sees it in their app. One source of truth, always current.

▼
The question everyone asks

Can everybody see my calendar? No. Nobody can.

This is not a second calendar to manage, and it is not calendar sharing. The platform reads busy or free, and nothing else, from the Google, Outlook or iCloud calendar each writer already uses. It shows one thing: the blocks where everyone in the room is open. Not what anyone is doing, not who they are meeting, not their week. When a session gets booked, it writes that one event back to everyone’s calendar. That is the entire exchange.
Three private calendars in, one list of mutual open blocks out. The green rows are the only thing that ever surfaces.
The real booking screen. Only mutual open blocks, never anyone’s calendar. Tap to expand.

For the songwriter in the app

Write, schedule and keep splits straight in one place.
  • Never chase a split sheet again — it's generated and signed in-app the day of the session.
  • Co-writes, calendar and catalog all in one app, synced across phone, laptop and iPad.
  • Your writer profile and stats update themselves as you connect and cut songs.

For the publisher / manager in the portal

See the whole roster without asking anyone for an update.
  • A live view of who's writing with whom and what's landing — no status emails.
  • Book rooms and target artists from proven data, then send the invite in a tap.
  • Splits and ownership visible the moment a session ends — no spreadsheets to reconcile.

The point: manage it once.

Nothing lives in two places. What a writer does in the app shows up here; what you do here shows up in their app. That's the whole idea.
